tier_reason: Table 7 of ePrint 2022/116 compares Rocca, built into OpenSSL, with OpenSSL AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 on a named CPU (i7-1068NG7). ePrint 2022/116 is the full version and a major revision of the peer-reviewed ToSC 2021(2) paper, and that paper shows the same win (138.22 vs 30.59 Gbps). Tier A is impossible: the benchmark harness is not public and neither version states a compiler or flags. The only code is the reference C in Appendix C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 16384B AEAD on i7-1068NG7 (Table 7): Rocca 150.95 Gbps vs OpenSSL AES-256-GCM 29.08 Gbps (~5.2x, derived from page data) and vs ChaCha20-Poly1305 7.60 Gbps (~19.9x, derived from page data). The paper text says 4.16x faster than SNOW-V and 3.10x faster than AES-256-CTR at 16384B; both figures come from the encryption-only rows. The lead shrinks on other CPUs and for small messages. On the i9-11900 (Appendix A, Table 9), 16384B AEAD is 175.12 vs AES-256-GCM 117.60 Gbps (~1.5x, derived from page data), and Rocca is slower than AES-256-GCM at 256B (13.81 vs 15.57 Gbps) and at 64B (3.68 vs 4.51 Gbps). These numbers are for the revised Rocca (key feedforward in initialization). The original peer-reviewed ToSC 2021 paper reports 138.22 Gbps vs AES-256-GCM 30.59 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 7.57 Gbps at 16384B AEAD.
corrections.workload: Single-thread throughput in encryption-only and AEAD modes, messages 64B to 16384B, 13-byte associated data. AEAD mode repeats init, AD, encryption, tag and finalization for every message. Rocca, SNOW-V, Tiaoxin-346 and AEGIS (from SUPERCOP) were built into OpenSSL (latest PDF says 3.1.0-dev; the Jan 2022 revision says 3.0.0-alpha3-Dev) and compared with OpenSSL's AES-256-GCM/CTR/CBC, ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, and SNOW-V-GCM.
corrections.hardware: Main table (Table 7): Intel Core i7-1068NG7 @2.30GHz, 32GB RAM. Appendix A adds Intel i9-12900K, i9-11900 and i9-10910 (Windows 10 Pro / macOS Big Sur 11.4), plus ARM NEON builds on Apple M1, Apple A15 Bionic and Qualcomm Snapdragon 888.
corrections.license: CC BY (license of the ePrint 2022/116 paper; the reference implementation exists only in the paper's Appendix C)
corrections.stars_or_usage: Peer-reviewed in IACR ToSC 2021(2) (presented at FSE 2022). ePrint 2022/116 is the full version: 4 revisions, last on 2023-03-16. The only standalone code found is a third-party C implementation of the original Rocca, ericlagergren/rocca (BSD-3-Clause, 5 stars, last commit 2022-01-28, no benchmarks). The successor Rocca-S has separate implementations such as jedisct1/zig-rocca-s (MIT, 21 stars).
corrections.caveats: The numbers at benchmark_url (the latest ePrint PDF, 2023-03-16) are for the REVISED Rocca, which adds key feedforward in initialization after the Hosoyamada et al. ToSC 2022(3) attack: a full 256-bit key recovery with about 2^128 data and time, which breaks the original 256-bit claim. They are not for the original design. The original design's peer-reviewed numbers are in ToSC 2021(2): 138.22 vs 30.59 / 7.57 Gbps. Across ePrint revisions the OpenSSL baseline numbers stay identical to two decimals (AES-256-GCM 29.08 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 7.60 Gbps on the i7; 57.87 and 21.99 on the i9-12900K) while the OpenSSL version label and the Rocca numbers change. So the baselines were probably not re-measured. Compiler and flags are never stated. The advantage depends heavily on the CPU: only about 1.5x over AES-256-GCM on the i9-11900, and Rocca loses at 64B and 256B there. The code is C with AES-NI/NEON intrinsics, not C++. The design has since been superseded by Rocca-S.

notes: The record's name says 'original/pre-attack', but the numbers it cites (150.95 Gbps, OpenSSL 3.1.0-dev) belong to the revised Rocca in the 2023 ePrint revision. Either rename the entry to 'Rocca (revised, key feedforward)' or repoint benchmark_url to the ToSC 2021 paper (https://tosc.iacr.org/index.php/ToSC/article/download/8904/8480) and use its original-design numbers. The record's language field says C++, but the code is C. repo_url could point to ericlagergren/rocca (original Rocca, BSD-3-Clause), but that repo has no benchmarks.
